subject.title: Telegram: apiRoot local Bot API server receives updates but never dispatches to agent sessions

question: For Telegram local Bot API migrations, should OpenClaw reset or scope the persisted update offset when `apiRoot` changes, and should `400: Logged out` during the Telegram `logOut` cooldown be a narrow nonfatal startup state?
rationale: This choice changes persisted polling-state semantics and Telegram 4xx startup handling; automation should not choose between runtime reset, doctor migration, manual documentation, or fail-closed auth behavior without maintainer intent and live proof.

options.title: Endpoint-aware migration with narrow cooldown tolerance
options.body: Reset or scope the offset when the API root changes and tolerate only the documented `400: Logged out` migration cooldown while preserving fail-closed behavior for other auth errors.

options.title: Document manual reset only
options.body: Leave runtime state unchanged and document the exact offset cleanup steps required when moving a bot token from official Telegram API to a local Bot API server.

options.title: Keep current fail-closed behavior
options.body: Preserve the account/token offset and `deleteWebhook` 4xx behavior, accepting that local Bot API migrations remain operator-managed and can require manual recovery.

recommendation.title: Endpoint-aware migration with narrow cooldown tolerance
recommendation.body: Reset or scope the offset when the API root changes and tolerate only the documented `400: Logged out` migration cooldown while preserving fail-closed behavior for other auth errors.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work on Telegram isolated ingress spool recovery makes this the closest current owner path for polling-state behavior.
